title: Soup ship judge row
description: One pairwise judge verdict of `soup ship --task-mode pairwise --output FILE`, written to <FILE stem>.judge-rows.jsonl, one line per judged prompt: the task-eval prompts (leg task_eval) and, under --gate loop-v2, the held-out edits (leg held_out). The verdict JSON points at the file with its `judge_rows` field (a path relative to the verdict file). The judge saw each pair in both presentation orders; a side wins only when both orders pick it. The file holds your prompts and both models' answers in full: treat it like the inputs it came from. Rows are JSONL, so every line carries its own `schema_version` and there is no header line: a reader that meets a higher version it does not know skips the line, and a line is complete without the lines around it. The noise-floor repeats (the base judged against itself) are never recorded. Readers ignore unknown fields.

schema_version.description: Version of this row format. Present on every line.

leg.description: Which judge pass the row belongs to. task_eval: the --task-eval prompts (leg 1 of the verdict). held_out: the --held-out edits of --gate loop-v2 (the style note, which is information only and never decides).

index.description: The row's 0-based position in that leg's input.

id.description: The row's name: its edit_id or id when the input has one, else the full SHA-256 of its prompt as written (see id_source).

id_source.description: Where `id` came from. prompt_sha256: the input had no usable id, so `id` is the lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 of the prompt as written (not trimmed or case-folded).

prompt_hash.description: `prompt_hash` is the 12-hex key sha256(strip().casefold()) of the row's last user message, and is not the 64-hex hash of a whole messages list used elsewhere (the paraphrase format's `prompt_hash` is that one; do not compare the two). Precisely: the first 12 lowercase hex digits of the SHA-256 of `prompt` after strip() and casefold(), UTF-8 encoded. It is the key the loop's holdout split hashes, so it joins a row to the edit it judged.

prompt.description: The prompt the judge was shown, exactly.

base_answer.description: The old version's answer, exactly as the judge saw it (the base model, plus --base-adapter when given). Always the base side, whichever order the judge saw it in.

tuned_answer.description: The new version's answer, exactly as the judge saw it. Always the tuned side.

base_truncated.description: True when the base answer stopped because it used up the generation token cap (256 new tokens on leg task_eval, 512 on leg held_out) rather than because the model finished. Taken from the generation result, never guessed from the length of the text. null: the generator did not report it (never from Soup's own live generator).

tuned_truncated.description: The same for the tuned answer.

judge_model.description: The model name of the judge as --judge-model / eval.ship.judge_model configures it: the model part of the URL (llama3.1 for ollama://llama3.1, gpt-4o-mini for https://api.openai.com/gpt-4o-mini). The host and anything else in the URL are not copied.

base_first.description: Whom the judge picked when the base answer was shown first (as A). none: no pick, because the judge said tie or its reply could not be read.

tuned_first.description: Whom the judge picked when the tuned answer was shown first. none: as for base_first. null: the pair was judged in one order only (soup ship always judges both).

result.description: What the two orders came to. A side wins only when BOTH orders pick it; a disagreement, a tie or an unreadable reply is a tie.

tie_reason.description: Why a tie is a tie. null on a row that is not a tie; one of the three values on a tie. unreadable_reply: a judge reply could not be parsed in at least one order (checked first). real_tie: the judge answered tie in both orders. order_disagreement: both replies were read and the two orders do not name the same side (a pick in one and a tie in the other, or opposite picks, which is what a judge biased towards one position does).

score.description: The tuned side's share of the win rate: 1.0 tuned, 0.5 tie, 0.0 base. The mean of `score` over one leg is that leg's win rate.

^x_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: Producer extension namespace (x_<app>). Soup never reads or rewrites it.
